subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve elevated cron/heartbeat authority as a narrow per-job/heartbeat approval state, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance RFC?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the trust boundary for elevated host exec across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, heartbeat files/config, audit, migration, and upgrade behavior, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with explicit migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevation unless maintainers intentionally preserve a documented compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged cron caller-scope work makes joshavant the closest current owner path for scheduling provenance decisions.
